decisive_items: Later developed painful vesicular oral and genital lesions with low-grade fever
Hyperintensities in thalami, midbrain, and pons
Lymphocytic pleocytosis with mixed inflammatory cells
response.rationale: Recurrent oral and genital ulcerations with chronic fever, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis, and brainstem/thalamic MRI hyperintensities are characteristic of neuro-Behçet's; negative WNV IgM and autoimmune panel favor Behçet's over viral/autoimmune encephalitis.

rejected.why: Too nonspecific; Behçet's is the precise autoimmune/vasculitic diagnosis.
Autoimmune encephalitis panel was negative and mucocutaneous ulcers are not typical.
Too broad; does not explain the oral/genital ulcers and chronic course.
Negative WNV IgM argues against acute West Nile encephalitis and ulcers are atypical.
No Lyme-specific features; oral/genital ulcers are not characteristic.
Lacks sicca symptoms, genital ulcers, and fever pattern of this case.
CSF was negative for malignancy and mucocutaneous ulcers are not explained.
Generic viral meningoencephalitis does not account for chronic oral/genital ulcers and brainstem MRI pattern.
No pharyngitis/lymphadenopathy; MRI and ulcerative lesions are not mononucleosis features.
No syphilis serology or specific signs; oral/genital ulcers are not typical.
